extracted.name: Roasted Chicken Thighs with Honey Mustard and Apples
extracted.description: This is a really tasty weeknight dinner. The honey mustard adds some zing that is nicely balanced by the sweetness of the apples and onions. The gravy really brings it all together, too! This recipe is modified from The Food Network. #GlobalApron - Week 40. Apples, Honey #Dinner #Savory #Meat
ingredient_lines: 6-8 skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (2 to 2 1/2 pounds)
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
1 large sweet onion, cut into large chunks
2 cooking apples (see Notes), cut into chunks
1-2 tablespoons roughly chopped fresh parsley (for serving)
instruction_lines: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 450°F.
Chop the onion into large chunks. Cut the apples into slices that are about 3/4” wide, then chop them in half. Mince the garlic.

Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large skillet or a deep, wide pot over medium-high heat. Working in batches if necessary, add the chicken, skin-side down, and cook until golden, about 6 minutes.
Flip and cook 2 to 3 more minutes, then transfer to a plate. Pour off all but about 2 tablespoons of the drippings.

Add the onion and apples to the pot and season with salt, pepper, and ginger. Cook until slightly softened, about 4 minutes. When one minute is left in the cooking time, add the garlic and sauté, stirring everything together.
Mix the broth, honey mustard and honey in a bowl, then add to the pot and bring to a boil.
Pour the onion/apple/broth mixture into the 9x13 pan. Place the chicken, skin-side up, on top of this mixture.
Roast in the preheated oven until the chicken is cooked through, 15 to 20 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the butter and flour to form a paste.
Use a slotted spoon to transfer the chicken, apples, and onion to plates. Transfer the pan juices to a pot.

Whisk in about half of the butter-flour mixture to the pan juices and boil to thicken (about 2 minutes.) Continue to cook, adding more of the butter-flour mixture as needed to make a slightly thick gravy. Taste, and season with salt and pepper, if needed.
If not serving immediately, transfer the apples and onions to a storage container and layer the chicken on top. The gravy can be stored separately until use.
To serve, place the chicken on a small bed of apples/onions, and top with gravy. Sprinkle with parsley.
Notes: Cooking apples will hold their shape and not get too mushy after baking. Varieties include: Cortland, Honeycrisp, Granny Smith, Fuji, Jonamac, Gala, Empire, or Pink Lady.
